samples.aliases: hot-rolled and solution treated 10 min at 900°C

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cast plates hot rolled at 900 °C to an 84% reduction in thickness.
Solution treated for 10 min at 900 °C and then water quenched to produce an equiaxed austenite grain structure 10–20 µm in average diameter.

structures.overall_structure: Equiaxed austenite grain structure with average grain diameter 10–20 µm

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Wrought (hot-rolled) Fe-30Mn-9Al-1.01Si-0.9C-0.5Mo, solution treated 900 °C 10 min, water quenched

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: ductility at equivalent ultimate tensile strength

characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructure characterization of the wrought sample
characterization_methods.key_findings: Equiaxed austenite grain structure, 10–20 µm average grain diameter; Fig. 6 also shows preferential grain-boundary etching from κ-carbide precipitation and banding from alloy segregation in the peak-aged condition.

characterization_methods.purpose: Tensile properties (UTS, elongation) as a function of aging time; wrought vs cast comparison
characterization_methods.key_findings: Solution-treated (0.1 h) wrought UTS between 900 and 1000 MPa; elongation 54% in solution-treated condition; tensile strength increased by 200 MPa with aging; peak aging lowered elongation to 14%.

unmapped_findings: The wrought sample is a calcium-treated, low-phosphorus (0.006% P) Fe-30Mn-9Al-1.01Si-0.9C-0.5Mo steel (b0039–b0040).
Tensile strength in the wrought alloy increased by 200 MPa with aging (b0040).

Note: b0040 states the 10–20 µm equiaxed grain structure is shown in Fig. 6, but the Fig. 6 caption describes the peak-aged condition (60 h at 530 °C) with grain-boundary κ-carbide precipitation; the 10–20 µm grain-size value is taken from the text.
